title: Ukrainian Drones Set Russia's Fourth-Largest Refinery Ablaze in Kstovo, 800km from the Border
detail: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a drone strike overnight into August 26 on Lukoil's NORSI refinery in Kstovo, Nizhny Novgorod Oblast — roughly 800km from the Ukrainian border. The facility, Russia's fourth-largest oil refinery and second-largest gasoline producer with a capacity of 15–17 million tonnes of crude a year, caught fire after the impact. President Zelensky said Ukraine struck 16 targets across Russia that day, including oil facilities, military installations, and logistics hubs. NORSI has been hit repeatedly through 2026, with prior strikes on April 5, May 20, June 24, and July 2.

title: Ukrainian Drones Destroy Wildberries Warehouse in Tambov Region; 3 Killed Across Russia
detail: An overnight Ukrainian drone strike on August 26 destroyed a Wildberries logistics center in Kotovsk, Tambov Oblast, roughly 500km southeast of Moscow — Tambov Governor Yevgeny Pervyshov said about 100,000 square meters of the facility were 'completely destroyed by fire,' the equivalent of 14 football pitches. It was the second strike on the facility since a July attack. At least 3 people were reportedly killed across Russia in the broader overnight campaign: a man and a 14-year-old in Lipetsk Oblast from a fire sparked by a falling drone, and a woman in Belgorod Oblast. President Zelensky said the strikes were part of a 16-target overnight campaign against Russian oil, logistics, and military infrastructure, part of Ukraine's stated policy of pushing 'the cost of the war for the aggressor' higher.

title: Russian Guided Bomb Seriously Damages Kherson's Main Heating Plant
detail: Russian forces struck the Kherson combined heat and power plant with a guided aerial bomb on August 26, seriously damaging the city's main source of heat, Naftogaz Group said. The plant is exclusively a civilian facility supplying heat to Kherson residents and has been hit by Russian attacks dozens of times through 2026; a full damage assessment was pending as of the report, with Naftogaz saying it would resume once the security situation allowed.
